issues.legal_issue: A decree may not be rectified to add settlement terms when the court did not intend to include them in the original decree and their omission was not an accidental or clerical error.
material_facts: The original joint petition sought a decree dissolving the marriage; although it referred to an agreement and asked that it be treated as part of the petition, its prayer did not seek incorporation of the agreement’s terms into the decree.
The decree dissolved the marriage and did not mention the agreement or its terms.

A later application sought mandatory injunctions and other reliefs, but did not ask for the agreement’s terms to be incorporated into the decree; it attributed the omission to the parties’ failure to request those reliefs while appearing without lawyers.
The Family Court nevertheless amended the decree to include all the agreement’s terms, although the record did not show that the court had intended to include them when making the original decree.
issues.conclusion: The amendment was not a correction of a clerical error or accidental slip. The Supreme Court allowed the appeal, set aside the orders allowing amendment, and held that the rectification application should be dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 152 of the Code of Civil Procedure permits correction of clerical or arithmetical mistakes and errors arising from an accidental slip or omission so that the decree reflects what the court originally intended. The power, including the court’s inherent power to correct such mistakes, cannot be used to reconsider the merits or add to or alter the decree where no original judicial intention to include the omitted matter is established. The Court relied on the maxim actus curiae neminem gravabit and Assam Tea Corporation Ltd. v. Narayan Singh; I.L. Janakirama Iyer v. P.M. Nilakanta Iyer; Bhikhi Lal v. Tribeni; Master Construction Co. (P) Ltd. v. State of Orissa; Dwarakadas v. State of M.P.; Thirugnanavalli Ammal v. P. Venugopala Pillai; Maharaj Puttu Lal v. Sripal Singh; State of Bihar v. Nilmani Sahu; and Bai Shakriben v. Special Land Acquisition Officer.

rule.if: appeal_from_decree_rectification_order and original_petition_sought_only_primary_relief and decree_omitted_additional_terms and later_application_did_not_seek_incorporation and original_court_intention_unshown

predicates.appeal_from_decree_rectification_order: A party appealed from an order rectifying or amending a decree.
predicates.original_petition_sought_only_primary_re: The original petition’s requested relief was limited to the principal remedy and did not request the additional terms later added to the decree.
predicates.decree_omitted_additional_terms: The original decree did not include the additional terms at issue.
predicates.later_application_did_not_seek_incorpora: The later application sought other relief but did not request that the omitted terms be incorporated into the decree.
predicates.original_court_intention_unshown: The record did not show that the court intended to include the additional terms when it made the original decree.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a decree amendment, the original request was limited, the decree omitted additional terms, the later application did not ask to incorporate them, and the original court’s intention to include them is unshown, rectification is not permitted.
